old: - `scrum-guide-2020-stakeholder-engagement.md`, Ken Schwaber & Jeff Sutherland (The Scrum Guide, November 2020). The canonical primary source for Scrum's engagement structure: Product Owner as single conduit for external stakeholders; Sprint Review as dedicated stakeholder ceremony (working session, not presentation; Product Backlog adjustable in the room); Sprint Retrospective as team-internal engagement (individuals, interactions, processes, tools, Definition of Done); Daily Scrum as Developer-only Sprint-Goal coordination; Scrum Master serving three principals (Scrum Team, Product Owner, organisation) including "removing barriers between stakeholders and Scrum Teams"; Scrum Values (Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect, Courage) as engagement conditions; Product Goal as long-term engagement anchor; Increment may be released to stakeholders before Sprint Review; Definition of Done as shared stakeholder commitment. Applies to "essentially complex work" beyond software. **CC BY-SA 4.0 — copyleft propagation.** Framework-level rather than methods-level; pairs with Letaw for methods inside the framework and with OpenStax *Business Ethics* (Mitchell-Agle-Wood) for the stakeholder-mapping theory the Guide does not provide.
new: - `scrum-guide-2020-stakeholder-engagement.md`, Ken Schwaber & Jeff Sutherland (The Scrum Guide, November 2020). Applies to "essentially complex work" beyond software. **CC BY-SA 4.0 — copyleft propagation.** Framework-level rather than methods-level; pairs with Letaw for methods inside the framework and with OpenStax *Business Ethics* (power × interest prioritisation, Grunig-Hunt categories) for the stakeholder-mapping theory the Guide does not provide.
why: Mitchell-Agle-Wood is not in the Business Ethics deep ref; it carries a power × interest matrix (Ch 3.3) and Grunig-Hunt categories (Ch 3.2) (distillation D009)
